chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one person, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Ali عليه السلام would not go beyond cutting the hand and the foot, and he would say: “Indeed, I feel shame before my Lord to leave him with nothing by which he may cleanse himself or purify himself.”
He said: And I asked him, if he steals after the hand and foot have been cut, he said: “I would commit him to prison forever and spare the people from his harm.”

key_terms.أَسْتَحْيِي: I feel shame; an expression of reverence before Allah
key_terms.الرِّجْلِ: the foot, mentioned here as part of the punishment for repeated theft
key_terms.قَطْعِ الْيَدِ: the amputation of the hand as a prescribed punishment for theft
key_terms.يَتَطَهَّرُ: to purify oneself ritually or physically
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: to clean oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a thief who steals again after the hand and foot have already been cut?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling attributed to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام regarding repeated theft: the hadd punishment is not increased beyond cutting the hand and the foot. After that, if the person steals again, he is imprisoned permanently in order to protect society, while preserving for him the means of basic purification.
